frontmatter.title: Fourier transform and phase estimation
frontmatter.description: Explicit exact and approximate Fourier circuits, textbook phase estimation, feedback QPE and conditional resource scaling.

children.value: Many quantum tasks encode the answer in an eigenphase: an energy in Hamiltonian evolution, an order in modular arithmetic, or a probability in amplitude amplification. A phase is not directly visible in a computational-basis measurement. Phase estimation uses controlled evolution and interference to turn it into a classical binary record

The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) combines the phases carried by a register. Phase estimation first prepares a superposition of different evolution lengths, then applies an inverse QFT so that matching phases add and mismatching phases cancel. QFT produces a quantum state; it does not return every entry of a classical Fourier transform in one measurement. This chapter supplies reusable components for the survey’s applications

children.value: The arbitrary-angle T cost is an empirical mean fit for random angles, not a concrete synthesis sequence, per-angle worst-case bound or runtime-tail certificate. QDK abstracts Clifford scheduling and factory work. Consequently these physical numbers do not certify the ideal phase-confidence contract on hardware. Algorithmic resolution, coherent synthesis approximation, ideal statistical failure and modeled physical faults remain separate. Classical processing, external loading and application-specific state preparation outside the supplied circuits are excluded. These circuit families do not modify or claim to improve the

Generation is capped at 64 total wires, 16 phase bits, 200,000 source operations and 1,000,000 decomposed export operations. QFT matrix checks are capped at eight wires, static statevector checks at 14 total wires, and feedback instrument checks at eight quantum/classical bits and 4,096 top-level operations. A circuit generated with
is explicitly unvalidated at that size.

The dedicated QFT/QPE suite has 104 cases covering exact transform matrices for one through six wires, inverses, all tested truncation cutoffs, grid and off-grid phases, bit order, coherent global phases, phase mixtures, actual feedback/reset behavior, primitive lowering and rejected opaque/dynamic access. The reference Fourier matrix and Dirichlet distribution are independent mathematical constructions. Additional independent review checked conjugated multi-qubit eigenstates and entangled phase mixtures. These numerical checks cover the tested instances; they are not a theorem for every generator input.
No Lean formalization is integrated or claimed.
